IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p150/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p150/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p150/r3.claim: The repeated warning is cited as an emphatic repetition.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p150/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p150/r8.speaker: عوف بن الخرع
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p150/r8.claim: ʿAwf ibn al-Kharaʿ repeats أولى in his line about Fazāra to illustrate emphatic repetition.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p150/r8.anchor:
وقال عوف بن الخرع :
وكادت فزارة تصلي بنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r1.claim: The warning outlines woe at death, at Resurrection, and on entering Hell, mapping successive punishments.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r1.anchor: والويلُ لك ميتاً، والويل لك يوم البعث، والويل لك يوم تدخل النار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r2.claim: Fa separates each pair of closely spaced punishments, while thumma marks the distant interval between worldly death, the grave, Resurrection, and Hell; immediate fa also matches the surah's haste theme.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p234/r2.anchor: فكل عذابين قريبين من بعضهما فصل بينهما بالفاء

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r5.claim: It repeats the same warning formula twice.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r5.anchor: وكررت آية واحدة مرتين وهي قوله: {أولى لَكَ فأولى * ثُمَّ أولى لَكَ فأولى}

NAHHAS:v5p92/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p92/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p92/r13.claim: This expression is said to someone who has fallen into ruin or come close to it.
NAHHAS:v5p92/r13.anchor: يقال لمن وقع في هلكة أو قاربها

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r1.speaker: قتادة والكلبي ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r1.claim: Qatāda, al-Kalbī, and Muqātil report that Muhammad seized Abū Jahl’s hand and warned him; Abū Jahl boasted of his power, left, and the verse confirmed the warning.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r1.anchor: قال قتادة والكلبي ومقاتل : أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيد أبي جهل . ثم قال

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r2.claim: Awlā laka means “woe to you,” a curse calling for what the person dislikes to befall him.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى قوله : { أولى لك } بمعنى ويل لك ، وهو دعاء عليه ، بأن يليه ما يكرهه

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r3.claim: Al-Qāḍī explains it as separation and ruin for the person’s worldly and afterlife affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r3.anchor: قال القاضي : المعنى بعد ذلك ، فبعدا ( لك ) في أمر دنياك ، وبعدا لك ، في أمر أخراك

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r4.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r4.claim: Others take the phrase to mean woe to you once more after that.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون : المعنى الويل لك مرة بعد ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r5.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r5.claim: Al-Qaffāl’s first possibility is a fresh threat from God to unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r5.anchor: قال القفال : هذا يحتمل وجوها أحدها : أنه وعيد مبتدأ من الله للكافرين

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r6.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r6.claim: Al-Qaffāl’s second possibility is that Muhammad said it to his enemy, who scorned the threat from pride, so God revealed the same words.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r6.anchor: أنه شيء قاله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعدوه فاستنكره عدو الله لعزته عند نفسه ، فأنزل الله تعالى مثل ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl’s third possibility is a divine command that Muhammad tell the enemy to beware, since an unbearable misfortune is near.
RAZI-FULL:v30p206#2/r7.anchor: أن يكون ذلك أمرا من الله لنبيه ، بأن يقولها لعدو الله ، فيكون المعنى { ثم ذهب إلى أهله يتمطى } ( القيامة : 33 ) فقل له : يا محمد : { أولى لك فأولى } أي احذر

STUDYQURAN:75:34/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r1.claim: One rendering is “that to which you are averse is now nearer to you.”
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r1.anchor: These verses mean, “That to which you are averse is now nearer to you”

STUDYQURAN:75:34/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r2.speaker: Iṣ
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r2.claim: Another interpretation is that punishment is now nearer.
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r2.anchor: or the punishment is now nearer

STUDYQURAN:75:34/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r3.speaker: Ṭs, Z
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r3.claim: Some commentators render the repeated phrase as “woe to you” four times.
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r3.anchor: According to some commentators, vv. 34–35 could also be rendered, “So woe to you! And woe! Then woe to you! And woe!”

STUDYQURAN:75:34/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r4.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r4.claim: Some apply the woes to Abū Jahl: at Badr, in the grave, at resurrection, and in Hell.
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r4.anchor: This is then interpreted by some as a direct address to Abū Jahl

STUDYQURAN:75:34/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r5.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r5.claim: Alternatively, it addresses all disbelievers who reject and swagger arrogantly.
STUDYQURAN:75:34/r5.anchor: It can also be taken as a more general address to all those who disbelieve and swagger in arrogance

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r5.claim: The repeated threat intensifies the warning; ‘better for you’ predicates an omitted subject referring to his conduct, metonymically assigning its burden and punishment.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r5.anchor: لا ريب أنه كلمة تهديد كررت لتأكيد التهديد، ولا يبعد - والله أعلم - أن يكون قوله { أولى لك } خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف هو ضمير عائد إلى ما ذكر

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r6.claim: The threat is God’s word stamped on the person’s heart, barring faith and piety and decreeing that he be among the people of the Fire.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r6.anchor: كلمة طبع طبع الله بها على قلبه حرم بها الإيمان والتقوى وكتب عليه أنه من أصحاب النار

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r7.claim: The wording resembles 47:20; his present state leads him to taste its consequence and punishment.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r7.anchor: والآيتان تشبهان بوجه قوله تعالى فإذا أنزلت سورة محكمة وذكر فيها القتال رأيت الذين في قلوبهم مرض

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r8.claim: One view treats awla as an indeclinable ism fi‘l meaning ‘woe to you, evil after evil.’
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r8.anchor: وقيل أولى لك اسم فعل مبني ومعناه وليك شر بعد شر

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r9.claim: Another treats awla as a past optative from wali, with destruction as its hidden subject and an extra lām: ‘may destruction approach you.’
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r9.anchor: وقيل أولى فعل ماض دعائي من الولي بمعنى القرب وفاعل الفعل ضمير مستتر عائد إلى الهلاك واللام مزيدة

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r10.claim: Alternatively, God is the hidden subject and the lām is extra (‘God gives you what you hate’) or original (‘God brings you near what you hate’).
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r10.anchor: وقيل الفاعل ضمير مستتر راجع إليه تعالى

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r11.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r11.claim: Another gloss supplies an omitted word: blame is more fitting than leaving it unsaid; the phrase became like ‘woe to you.’
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r11.anchor: وقيل معناه الذم أولى لك من تركه إلا أنه حذف وكثر في الكلام حتى صار بمنزلة الويل لك

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r12.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r12.claim: A further gloss is ‘May God destroy you with a destruction nearer than every other evil and ruin.’
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r12.anchor: وقيل المعنى أهلكك الله هلاكا أقرب لك من كل شر وهلاك

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r13.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r13.claim: Another analysis takes awla as a comparative adjective with an omitted predicate: Hell is most fitting for you, or you deserve it.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r13.anchor: وقيل أولى أفعل تفضيل بمعنى الأحرى، وخبر لمبتدأ محذوف يقدر كما يليق بمقامه

TABATABAI:75:31-36/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r14.claim: The reported explanations are weak or strained; the last is close to the author’s reading but does not fully match it.
TABATABAI:75:31-36/r14.anchor: وهي وجوه ضعيفة لا تخلو من تكلف والوجه الأخير قريب مما قدمنا وليس به

TABRISI:75:29-36/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:75:29-36/r13.claim: The phrase threatens Abū Jahl that harm and destruction have drawn near to him.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r13.anchor: وهذا تهديد من الله له والمعنى وليك المكروه يا أبا جهل وقرب منك

TABRISI:75:29-36/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r14.speaker: رسول الله
TABRISI:75:29-36/r14.claim: A report says the Messenger took Abū Jahl's hand and repeated the threat; Abū Jahl boasted that neither the Messenger nor his Lord could harm him, so God revealed the verse as foretold.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r14.anchor: وجاءت الرواية أن رسول الله أخذ بيد أبي جهل ثم قال له:

TABRISI:75:29-36/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r15.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:75:29-36/r15.claim: One analysis supplies an omitted word: blame is more fitting for him than leaving it; frequent ellipsis made the phrase an idiom equivalent to woe, with the omitted wording no longer expressible.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r15.anchor: الذم أولى لك من تركه إلا أنه حذف وكثر في الكلام حتى صار بمنزلة الويل لك

TABRISI:75:29-36/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r16.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:75:29-36/r16.claim: Qatāda reads a threat upon a threat: evil comes to him in this world and then in the next, with repetition for emphasis.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r16.anchor: وقيل: هو وعيد على وعيد عن قتادة ومعناه وليك الشر في الدنيا وليك ثم وليك الشر في الآخرة

TABRISI:75:29-36/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r17.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:75:29-36/r17.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī glosses it as distance from the good things of this world and the next.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r17.anchor: وقيل: بعدا لك من خيرات الدنيا وبعدا لك من خيرات الآخرة عن الجبائي

TABRISI:75:29-36/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:29-36/r18.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:75:29-36/r18.claim: Another reading warns Abū Jahl of what he will witness at Badr, then in the grave, on Judgment Day, and in the Fire; thumma marks the sequence.
TABRISI:75:29-36/r18.anchor: أولى لك ما تشاهده يا أبا جهل يوم بدر فأولى لك في القبر ثم أولى لك يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v10p198/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p198/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p198/r5.claim: أولى لك is a threat wishing that what he dislikes draw near; it is used in the sense of ويل لك, “woe to you.”
BURSEVI:v10p198/r5.anchor: فهو مستعمل في موضع ويل لك مشتق من الولي وهو القرب

BURSEVI:v10p198/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p198/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p198/r6.claim: The repeated formula intensifies the threat.
BURSEVI:v10p198/r6.anchor: تكرير للتأكيد فهو مستعمل في موضع ويل لك مشتق من الولي

BURSEVI:v10p198/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p198/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p198/r7.claim: The threat may derive from “May God bring near to you what you hate,” with an added lām and a triliteral form shifted to ifʿāl to take two objects.
BURSEVI:v10p198/r7.anchor: وأصله أولاك الله ما تكرهه واللام مزيدة كما في ردف لكم

BURSEVI:v10p198/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p198/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p198/r8.claim: Al-Qāmūs gives two explanations: a warning that destruction approaches, or a noun meaning destruction is more fitting and preferable for you.
BURSEVI:v10p198/r8.anchor: أولى لك تهديد ووعيد أي قاربه ما يهلكه

BURSEVI:v10p198/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p198/r9.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p198/r9.claim: Kāshifī assigns the repetitions escalating fates: a hard death, painful grave punishment, the horrors of resurrection, then eternal residence in Hell.

THALABI:v10p91/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p91/r1.claim: The repeated phrase is God's threat to Abu Jahl, a fixed expression of menace and warning.
THALABI:v10p91/r1.anchor: أولى لك فأولى ثم أولى لك فأولى هذا وعيد من الله سبحانه على وعيد أبي جهل وهي كلمة موضوعة للتهدد والوعيد

THALABI:v10p91/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r2.speaker: الخنساء
THALABI:v10p91/r2.claim: Al-Khansaʾ's verse uses awla as a word of threat to oneself.
THALABI:v10p91/r2.anchor: قالت الخنساء: هممت بنفسي كل الهموم … فأولى لنفسي أولى لها

THALABI:v10p91/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r3.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى بن تغلب
THALABI:v10p91/r3.claim: A verse recited to Thaʿlabī uses “awla fa-awla laka” as a threat in its address to Aws.
THALABI:v10p91/r3.anchor:
أنشدنا أحمد بن يحيى بن تغلب:
يا أوس لو نالتك أرماحنا … كنت

THALABI:v10p91/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r4.speaker: بعض العلماء
THALABI:v10p91/r4.claim: Some scholars explain awla as “you are more deserving and entitled” to the punishment that befalls you.
THALABI:v10p91/r4.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: معناه أنك أجدر بهذا العذاب وأحق وأولى، يقال للرجل يصيبه مكروه يستوجبه

THALABI:v10p91/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r5.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v10p91/r5.claim: Alternatively, it is an Arab expression for someone nearing misfortune, from wali meaning nearness; the author cites verses using yali for those nearby.
THALABI:v10p91/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو كلمة يقولها العرب لمن قاربه المكروه وأصلها من الولي وهو القرب

THALABI:v10p91/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r6.speaker: أبو الهيثم الجمي
THALABI:v10p91/r6.claim: Abu al-Haytham al-Jummi, citing a scholar, treats awla as an inversion of awyl, from wayl, like other inverted Arabic forms.
THALABI:v10p91/r6.anchor: سمع أبا الهيثم الجمي وكان عارفا بالمعاني يقول حاكيا عن بعض العلماء: أن قوله أولى من المقلوب

THALABI:v10p91/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p91/r7.claim: On this derivation the threat means: woe to Abu Jahl at death, resurrection, and entry into Hell, where he remains.
THALABI:v10p91/r7.anchor: ومعنى الآية كأنه يقول لأبي جهل: الويل لك يوم تموت، والويل لك يوم تبعث

THALABI:v10p91/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r8.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p91/r8.claim: Qatada recounts the Prophet seizing Abu Jahl's garment at al-Batḥa and threatening him; Abu Jahl boasted, but was killed at Badr by the two sons of ʿAfra and Ibn Masʿud.
THALABI:v10p91/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذكر لنا أن النبي (عليه السلام) لما نزلت هذه الآية أخذ بمجامع ثوب أبي جهل بالبطحاء

THALABI:v10p91/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r9.speaker: أبو جهل
THALABI:v10p91/r9.claim: The account says Abu Jahl claimed that had he known Muhammad was God's messenger, he would not have followed a Quraysh youth.
THALABI:v10p91/r9.anchor: قال: وذكر لنا أن أبا جهل كان يقول: لو علمت أن محمدا رسول الله ما أتبعت غلاما من قريش

THALABI:v10p91/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p91/r10.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v10p91/r10.claim: The Prophet called Abu Jahl the Pharaoh of this community, saying every community has a Pharaoh.
THALABI:v10p91/r10.anchor: قال: وذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: «إن لكل أمة فرعونا وأن فرعون هذه الأمة أبو جهل

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r7.claim: Such a man will not be among the laughing faces: he will suffer a dire fate, with his back broken and a dark, distressed face.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r7.anchor: Şüphe yok ki bu adam o gün gülecek yüzlerden değil. Kendilerine fâkıre[^2] yapılacak

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r8.claim: The Arabic idiom is a prayer of vindication, like Turkish “this calamity was deserved—serve you right.”
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r8.anchor: Arapça’da أَوْلَىٰ لَكَ tâbiri Türkçemizde “gerekti sana bu belâ oh olsun!” demek gibi bir dua ve teşeffî makamında kullanılır.

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r9.claim: Elmalılı relates awlā laka to awlā as “more fitting for you”: woe and destruction are what befit you.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r9.anchor: Mâlumumuz olan اَوْلٰى’dan اَوْلٰى لَكَ اَلْوَيْل “evlâ ve elyaktır sana o veyl ü helâk” mânasınadır.

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r10.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r10.claim: An alternative derives awlā from wayl by inversion, meaning that the greatest woe should befall him.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r10.anchor: Bazıları da bu وَتَوَلَّىٰ’nın ويل kelimesinden maklub olarak “en büyük veyl başına olsun” demek olduğunu söylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r11.claim: A report mentioned earlier says this verse was revealed about Abu Jahl.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r11.anchor: Bu âyetin Ebû Cehil hakkında nâzil olduğu rivayeti geçmişti.

ELMALILI:75:31-35/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r12.claim: Although reported about Abu Jahl, the verse plainly applies to others with the same traits.
ELMALILI:75:31-35/r12.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh mazmûnun[^3] emsâline de şümûlü zâhir olduğunda şüphe yoktur.

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after 74:30 was revealed, Abu Jahl mocked Quraysh over the nineteen Hell guardians; God directed the Prophet to confront him with the warning in 75:34–35.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224#2/r2.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير من طريق العوفي عن ابن عباس قال لما نزلت ﴿ عليها تسعة عشر ﴾

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224#2/r3.claim: In Saʿid ibn Jubayr’s question, Ibn Abbas says the Prophet first uttered this warning on his own, then God revealed it.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p224#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج النسائي عن سعيد بن جبير أنه سأل ابن عباس عن قوله أولى لك فأولى

DAMGHANI:v1p496/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p496/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p496/r2.claim: Here awlā is a threat to Abū Jahl, one warning added to another.
DAMGHANI:v1p496/r2.anchor: أولى لك فأولى ثم أولى لك فأولى أي وعيد لك يا أبا جهل على وعيد

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p501#4/r1.claim: The phrase is a threat and a warning.

SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r1.claim: The threat was discussed fully at the end of Surat Muhammad; its repetition here intensifies the warning and threat.
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r1.anchor: وتقدم الكلام على قوله: { أولى لك فأولى } في آخر سورة القتال مشبعا، وإنما كرر هنا مبالغة في التهديد والوعيد

SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r2.speaker: الخنساء
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r2.claim: Al-Khansa uses أولى لنفسي أولى لها as a poetic parallel for the expression.
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r2.anchor: وقالت الخنساء: 4426 هممت بنفسي كل الهموم فأولى لنفسي أولى لها

SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa gives two morphological accounts: فعلى with an alif of augmentation, or أفعل; on either account it is a proper name and therefore uninflected.
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r3.anchor: وزن أولى فيه قولان، أحدهما: فعلى، والألف فيه للإلحاق لا للتأنيث، والثاني: هو أفعل

SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r4.claim: Abu Zayd's report هي أولاة, with feminine ت and no declension, is cited as evidence for the proper-name analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r4.anchor: ما حكى أبو زيد في " النوادر ": " هي أولاة " بالتاء غير مصروف

SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r5.claim: On the proper-name analysis, أولى is the subject and لك its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r5.anchor: فعلى هذا يكون " أولى " مبتدأ، و " لك " الخبر

SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r6.claim: Alternatively, أولى is a built-in imperative noun meaning one evil after another is coming to you, while لك is explanatory.
SAMIN-DURR:75:34/r6.anchor: أن يكون اسما للفعل مبنيا ومعناه: وليك شر بعد شر، و " لك " تبيين

ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r4.claim: The phrase means that harm is close to you, Abū Jahl; Arabs use awlā for someone as a curse invoking harm.
ZAJJAJ:v5p254/r4.anchor: معناه - والله أعلم - وليك المكروه يا أبا جهل، والعرب تقول أولى لفلان

ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r4.claim: The passage warns that man's end comes hourly nearer and nearer.
ASAD-NOTES:75:31/r4.anchor: and ever nearer unto thee, and nearer

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r3.claim: Awlā laka is a warning and threat meaning ‘woe to you’; from w-l-y, nearness, its comparative form suggests destruction is close.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r3.anchor: واشتقاقها من (الوَلْي) وهو القرب، فهو اسم تفضيل يفيد قرب وقوع الهلاك

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r4.speaker: الكشاف
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r4.claim: Al-Kashshāf glosses the related awlā lahum as a threat meaning woe, from nearness, a prayer that misfortune come close to them.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r5.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r5.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī explains the phrase as a comparative originally, used for approaching ruin and a prayer for evil to be near.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r6.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī's usage in al-Ṣiḥāḥ takes the expression to mean that what destroys someone has drawn near.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r6.anchor: وفي الصحاح عن الأصمعي، قاربه ما يهلكه: أي نزل به

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r7.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r7.claim: Another reported view treats awlā as a fixed verbal expression meaning one evil follows another.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p227/r7.anchor: وقيل: اسم فعل مبني ومعناه: وليك شر بعد شر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r1.claim: The urgent threat fits people who chose immediate pleasures and sins and delayed obedience: just as they hurried into sin, ruin is hurried toward them, within the sūra's theme of haste.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r1.anchor: فهو مناسب لإيثارهم العاجلة وتقديمهم الفجور والشهوات وتأخيرهم الطاعات، فكما عجّلوا في فجورهم وشهواتهم ومعاصيهم عجل لهم الويل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r2.claim: Unlike Muhammad's single warning, this passage repeats awlā inside the verse and repeats the whole verse, repeats awlā but not laka, separates the inner warnings with fa, and separates the verses with thumma.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r2.anchor: إنه كرر الدعاء في سورة القيامة في الآية الواحدة فقال: {أولى لَكَ فأولى}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r3.claim: The different wording follows different contexts: Muhammad depicts hesitant people facing the prospect of fighting, while Qiyāma describes a denier who rejects faith and prayer and walks off arrogantly.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p228/r3.anchor: وبالتأمل في السياقين نجد السبب واضحاً. قال تعالى في سورة محمد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r4.claim: The Muhammad group are described while alive, when repentance remains possible; the Qiyāma person is described after death, having died in denial and facing the realized threat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r4.anchor: إن المذكورين في سورة محمد أخبر عنهم وهم أحياء، والأحياء تُرْجى لهم التوبة، وبابُ التوبة مفتوح

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r5.claim: Muhammad names one trait, cowardice before fighting, so the threat occurs once; Qiyāma names multiple forms of disbelief, warranting repeated threats.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p229/r5.anchor: ذكر في آية سورة محمد صفة واحدة، وهي الجبن عن القتال، فهدَّدهم مرة واحدة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r1.claim: Each of the two faults first receives a warning; the second verse restates them as denial and turning away, so the author counts four warnings, one for each fault in both formulations.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p230/r1.anchor: فلا صدق ... أولى لك. ولا صلى ... فأولى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r2.claim: The stronger ‘awlā laka’ answers unbelief, while the threat for not praying omits laka; the difference marks the gravity of faith, though the verse ending also supports the omission.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p231/r2.anchor: فقال مقابل {فَلاَ صَدَّقَ} {أولى لَكَ} فذكر {لَكَ} ومقابل {وَلاَ صلى} {فأولى} بحذف (لك) إشارة إلى عظم الإيمان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r1.claim: Thumma can mark distance in rank, not only time: the Qur'anic example in 90:11–17 distinguishes freeing and feeding from faith, so the later threat is more forceful.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r1.anchor: فما بعد (ثم) أبعد من الرتبة مما قبلها، وكذلك ههنا فإن التهديد أقوى من الأول

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r2.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r2.claim: A reported view says the repetition intensifies the warning and threat.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r2.anchor: وقيل: إن التكرار ههنا مبالغة في التهديد والوعيد

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r3.speaker: روح المعاني
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r3.claim: Rūḥ al-Maʿānī says the repeated phrase is for emphasis; thumma can also reinforce the statement, as in repeating an oath.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r4.claim: Thumma may also indicate temporal delay between punishment in the grave and punishment in the Hereafter, as in Pharaoh's people.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p232/r4.anchor: وربما جاء بـ (ثم) للتراخي الزمني أيضاً، إذ هناك عذاب في القبر وعذاب في الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r2.claim: Adding “لك” to the first warning and omitting it from the second matches the stronger threat to disbelief and signals that the two failings differ in gravity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r2.anchor: فذكر (لك) ومقابل (ولا صلّى) قال (فأولى) بحذف (لك) إشارة إلى عظم الإيمان وأهميته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r4.claim: The later “denied and turned away” restates the lack of belief and prayer; each is reinforced and receives its own warning, yielding four threats.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p684/r4.anchor: وجاء (كذّب) مقابل (لا صدّق) و (تولّى) مقابل (لا صلّى)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p682/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p682/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p682/r3.claim: Qur'anic repetition is part of its inimitability; the first clause is joined by fa, and the second verse joins with thumma.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p682/r3.anchor: الآية فيها عطف على جزء من الآية بالفاء ثم عطف بـ (ثمّ) في الآية الثانية.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.claim: The disbelievers face an exacting journey without provisions: they neither prayed nor spent in God’s way, the two deeds that would benefit them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p82/r1.anchor: no resources and provisions to take along.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r3.claim: Wayl expresses anger, reproach, and hatred and is common in classical Arabic; Khansā’s verse illustrates this reproach, while translating it as “befitting” violates Arabic usage and context.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r3.anchor: which is used for expressing anger, reproach, and hatred.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r4.claim: The shift from indirect speech to direct address conveys sorrow and hatred.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p84/r4.anchor: In the previous verses, the address was indirect. Here in these verses the address has become direct.

NASHR:v2p81/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p81/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p81/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr opens the listed non-verse-final words on the routes that incline verse endings; for موسى he follows his usual between-vowels reading where imāla is transmitted.
NASHR:v2p81/r7.anchor: فإن أبا عمرو يفتح جميع ذلك من طريق المميلين له رءوس الآي لأنه ليس برأس آية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r2.claim: Qatāda recounts that the Prophet took Abū Jahl by the hand and addressed him with the warning; Abū Jahl defied him, then at Badr boasted that God would no longer be worshipped and was killed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r2.anchor: قال وهو أبو جهل كانت مشيته فأخذ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده فقال ﴿ أولى لك فأولى ثم أولى لك فأولى ﴾

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r3.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Muhammad first uttered “awlā laka,” and the Qurʾān was then revealed with the phrase.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#8/r3.anchor: سألت سعيد بن جبير قوله تعالى ﴿ أولى لك فأولى ﴾ قاله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي جهل أم نزل به القرآن فقال قاله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r12.claim: A report says the Messenger seized Abu Jahl at al-Baṭḥā and said God tells him أولى فأولى لك; the Quran was revealed in corresponding terms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p352/r12.anchor: روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لبب أبا جهل يوما في البطحاء وقال له: «إن الله يقول لك أولى فأولى لك»

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r1.claim: Awla is originally a comparative from proximity, but became a threat of approaching destruction: “destruction is nearer to you,” like سحقا in ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r1.anchor: أولى لك فأولى من الولي بمعنى القرب فهو للتفضيلفي الأصل غلب فيقر بالهلاكودعاء الس كأنه قيل هلاكاأولى لك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r2.claim: Al-Asma‘i glosses the threat as nearing what will destroy a person and cites poetry where أولى means “nearer.”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r2.anchor: وفي الصحاح عن الأصمعي قاربه ما يهلكه أينزلبه وأنشد فعادى بينهاديتينمنها وأولى أننزيد على الثلاث

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r3.claim: On the al-Asma‘i analysis, أولى is a verb with an implicit subject, destruction; the lām is said by some to be extra.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r3.anchor: وعلى هذاأولى فعل مستتر فيهضمير الهلاكبقرينة ال واللاممزيدة على ماقيل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r4.claim: Another analysis makes أولى a past-tense imprecation, with God as subject: may He bring what you hate near or bring destruction close to you.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r4.anchor: وقيلهوفعلماضدعائي منالولي أيضا إلا أن الفاعلضميره تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r5.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r5.claim: Abu Ali proposes that أولى is a proper name for ruin, patterned on أفعل by metathesis from أويل, and indeclinable for definiteness and pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r5.anchor: وعن أبيعلي إن أولى لك علم للويل مبني على زنة أفعلمن لفظالويلعلى القلبوأصله أويل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r6.claim: Al-Alusi objects that الويل is already indeclinable, that the analogy with يوم أيوم is nonstandard, and that metathesis or a generic proper name lacks clear grounds.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r6.anchor: لا يرتكبإلا بدليلوإن علم الجنس شيء خارج عن القياسمشكل التعقل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r7.speaker: قائلون
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r7.claim: A favored alternative treats أولى as a comparative meaning “more fitting”: the implied subject is fire, and the addressee deserves it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p149/r7.anchor: واختار جمع أنه أفعل تفضيل بمعنى الأحسن والأحرى خبر لمبتدأ محذوف يقدر كما يليق بمقامه فالتقدير هنا النار أولى لك أي أنت أحق بها وأهل لها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r15.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r15.claim: The repeated formula is God's threat and warning to Abu Jahl, repeated as a second threat.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r15.anchor: هذا وعيد على وعيد من الله عز وجل لأبي جهل، وهي كلمة موضوعة للتهديد والوعيد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r16.speaker: بعض العلماء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r16.claim: Some scholars gloss it as being more fit, deserving, or entitled to this punishment, said of someone who suffers what he merits.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r16.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: معناه أنك أجدر بهذا العذاب وأحق وأولى به،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r17.speaker: العرب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r17.claim: It is also an Arab expression for someone nearing harm, from walāʾ or mawlā meaning nearness, as in the command to fight those nearest among the disbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r17.anchor: وقيل: هي كلمة تقولها العرب لمن قاربه المكروه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r18.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r18.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r18.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet seized Abu Jahl's garment at al-Batha and recited the threat; Abu Jahl defied him, but was killed at Badr. The Prophet also called Abu Jahl this nation's Pharaoh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p286/r18.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نزلت هذه الآية أخذ بمجامع ثوب أبي جهل

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r3.claim: Awlā laka may mean woe or that God has brought near what he dislikes, with an extra lām as in 27:72; it may also mean perdition, be a form of al-wayl by metathesis, or describe the final return to the Fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r3.anchor: ويل لك من الولي، وأصله أولاك الله ما تكرهه

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r4.claim: The repeated warning returns to him again and again.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:32-36/r4.anchor: أي يتكرر ذلك عليه مرة بعد أخرى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r3.claim: This threat is the fitting reply in place of his family’s greeting: may God bring what he hates and strike him with one calamity after another.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r4.claim: The lām emphasizes the threat, its repetition across the two verses signals the enormity and enduring desert of the offense, and the successive calamities may be immediate or delayed and vary in severity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r4.anchor: وأبلغ ذلك التأكيد إشارة إلى أنه يستحقه على مدى الأعصار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r5.claim: Alternatively, the phrase urges him to leave his present conduct and turn to what benefits him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r5.anchor: أن تترك ما أنت عليه وتقبل على ما ينفعك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that after Abū Jahl mocked the nineteen keepers of Hell, God told the Prophet to meet him in Mecca and say these words to him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p255/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جرير في تفسير المدثر : إن أبا جهل لما استهزأ

DURR-FULL:v8p362/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r7.claim: Qatadah reports that the Prophet seized Abu Jahl by his garment and repeatedly warned him; Abu Jahl boasted that neither the Prophet nor his Lord could harm him and claimed supremacy between Mecca’s hills.
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r7.anchor: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله أخذ بمجامع ثوبه فقال: {أولى لك فأولى ثم أولى لك فأولى}

DURR-FULL:v8p362/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r8.claim: Qatadah reports the Prophet’s saying that every nation has a Pharaoh and Abu Jahl was this nation’s Pharaoh.
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r8.anchor: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله كان يقول: إن لكل أمة فرعونا وإن فرعون هذه الأمة أبو جهل

DURR-FULL:v8p362/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet first uttered the warning on his own initiative and God then revealed it.
DURR-FULL:v8p362/r11.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: سألت ابن عباس عن قول الله: {أولى لك فأولى} أشيء قاله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي جهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r1.claim: The fa makes the second imprecation follow immediately, threatening that harm will come after the first.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { فأولى } تأكيد ل { أولى لك } جيء فيه بفاء التعقيب للدلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r2.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet seized Abu Jahl at the mosque door and threatened him with this wording; Abu Jahl boasted of his strength, and the revelation answered him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r2.anchor: قال قتادة : إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج من المسجد فاستقبله أبو جهل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r4.claim: The warning concerns every disbeliever, as the passage's opening about resurrection and self-witness implies; Abu Jahl is one of the foremost examples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r4.anchor: وأحسب أن المراد : كل إنسان كافر كما يقتضيه أول الكلام من قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r5.claim: The Prophet used the revealed threat against Abu Jahl as a warning for people like him; early scholars' claims that an event occasioned revelation can be stated loosely.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p363#2/r5.anchor: وما أبو جهل إلا من أولهم ، وأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم توعده باللفظ الذي أنزله الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r14.claim: The author says the threat at 75:34–35 was then revealed about Abu Jahl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r14.anchor: فنزلت في أبي جهل: أولى لك فأولى [القيامة: 34- 35] الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.speaker: جمهور المتأولين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.claim: Most interpreters say the entire passage concerns Abu Jahl ibn Hisham.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r1.anchor: قال جمهور المتأولين: هذه الآية كلها إنما نزلت في أبي جهل بن هشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r8.claim: The second threat repeats the first for emphasis; أولى لك urges him to desist and stop, and Arabs use it as a rebuke, as in 47:20.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r8.anchor: وقوله تعالى: أولى لك وعيد ثان ثم كرر ذلك تأكيدا، والمعنى أولى لك الازدجار والانتهاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r9.claim: أولى is derived from ولي and is an Arabic formula of rebuke; al-Khansa's verse also illustrates its use.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r9.anchor: وهو مأخوذ من ولي، والعرب تستعمل هذه الكلمة زجرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r10.claim: A report says the Prophet held Abu Jahl at al-Bat'ha and told him that God says أولى لك فأولى, after which the Quran came in accord with it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r10.anchor: وروي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لبب أبا جهل يوما في البطحاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r11.claim: Al-Khansa uses أولى لنفسي أولى لها in poetry, demonstrating the expression's Arabic usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p406#2/r11.anchor: وفي شعر الخنساء: [المتقارب] سئمت بنفسي كل الهموم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#5/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#5/r1.claim: The expression is a threat and warning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#5/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة هو تهديد ووعيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#5/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#5/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#5/r2.claim: Arabs use awlā for someone they curse with misfortune; it means may misfortune befall you, Abu Jahl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p425#5/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج العرب تقول أولى لفلان إذا دعت عليه بالمكروه ومعناه وليك المكروه يا أبا جهل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r6.claim: The repeated words are a stern divine threat to the unbeliever who swaggered; their taunting tone says he deserves to walk proudly despite rejecting his Creator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r6.anchor: وهذا تهديد ووعيد أكيد منه تعالى للكافر به المتبختر في مشيته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r7.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r7.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports that the Prophet said these words to Abu Jahl, after which the Quran revealed them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p282#2/r7.anchor: قاله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي جهل، ثم نزل به القرآن.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r1.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Messenger spoke the warning and God then revealed it; this is another report of its occasion involving Abu Jahl.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r1.anchor: قاله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم (3) ثم أنزله الله عز وجل (4) .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r2.claim: Qatada calls the repeated warning a threat following another threat.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أولى لك فأولى ثم أولى لك فأولى} وعيد على أثر وعيد،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r3.claim: Qatada relays that Abu Jahl seized the Prophet by his clothes and repeated the warning, then mocked him, saying neither Muhammad nor his Lord could do anything and boasting that he was the mightiest in Mecca.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p283/r3.anchor: فقال عدو الله أبو جهل: أتوعدني يا محمد؟ والله لا تستطيع أنت ولا ربك شيئا،

JISHUMI:v10p7192/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r12.claim: One derivation takes awlā from walī, nearness, as in the command to fight those who are nearest to you.
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r12.anchor: قيل: أصله الولي، وهو القرب، ومنه: (قاتلوا الذين يلونكم)

JISHUMI:v10p7192/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r13.claim: Another explanation says awlā in an action means more entitled to it, and it also carries the sense of nearness.
JISHUMI:v10p7192/r13.anchor: وقيل: الأولى في الفعل هو الأحق، وهو أيضا من القرب

JISHUMI:v10p7193/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r1.claim: One occasion report says the verses concern Abū Jahl, who was killed at Badr in a terrible manner; a Prophetic report calls Abū Jahl the Pharaoh of this community.
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r1.anchor: نزلت الآيات في أبي جهل، وقتل يوم بدر شر مقتل، عن النبي

JISHUMI:v10p7193/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r2.claim: Another report says the Prophet met Abū Jahl outside the mosque and said awlā laka fa-awlā; Abū Jahl boasted that neither Muhammad nor his Lord could harm him, then went inside shaken, and the verse was revealed.
JISHUMI:v10p7193/r2.anchor: فاستقبله أبو جهل، فقال - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: (أولى لك فأولى) فقال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r8.claim: أولى لك means woe to you, a prayer that what you dislike should befall you.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p664#2/r8.anchor: بمعنى ويل لك ، وهو دعاء عليه بأن يليه ما يكره

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r28.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r28.claim: They report that the Prophet met swaggering Abu Jahl at Mecca’s Batha, pushed his chest and poked him while saying the warning; Abu Jahl taunted him, and the verses were revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r28.anchor: حكى الكلبي ومقاتل : أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لقي أبا جهل ببطحاء مكة وهو يتبختر

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r29.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r29.claim: One gloss is that evil is near to him; Qatada calls it one threat following another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r29.anchor: وليك الشر , قال قتادة , وهذا وعيد على وعيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r30.speaker: الخنساء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p157/r30.claim: A second gloss takes awla as woe to you, supported by al-Khansa’s poetic usage.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r1.speaker: الخنساء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r1.claim: Al-Khansa’s line uses awla in the sense of woe to oneself, supporting the preceding gloss.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r1.anchor: هممت بنفسي بعض الهموم … فأولى لنفسي أولى لها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r2.claim: Al-ala can mean a condition or circumstance, and also the bier on which the dead are carried.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p159/r2.anchor: الآلة : الحالة , والآلة : السرير أيضا الذي يحمل عليه الموتى

MUQATIL:75:34-40/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r1.claim: The repeated phrase is one threat following another because Abu Jahl threatened to kill the Prophet; Muhammad seized his lapels at Batḥa and shoved his chest.
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r1.anchor: { أولى لك فأولى ثم أولى لك فأولى } [آية: 35] يعني وعيدا على أثر وعيد، وذلك أن أبا جهل تهدد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالقتل، وأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخذ تلابيب أبي جهل بالبطحاء

MUQATIL:75:34-40/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r2.claim: Abu Jahl boasted that neither Muhammad nor his Lord could harm him, calling himself the strongest and most honored man of Batḥa, then left strutting.
MUQATIL:75:34-40/r2.anchor: فقال أبو جهل: إليك عني، فإنك لا تستطيع أنت ولا ربك أن تفعلا بى شيئا، لقد علمت قريش أنى أعز أهل البطحاء

NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#11/r1.claim: “أولى لك” means “woe to you” and curses him to meet what he hates.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p301#11/r1.anchor: بمعنى ويل لك وهو دعاء عليه بأن يليه ما يكره

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r7.claim: The repeated phrase is successive threat and warning, four warnings corresponding to four faults in Abu Jahl.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r7.anchor: تهديد بعد تهديد، ووعيد بعد وعيد، أي فهو وعيد أربعة لأربعة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.claim: The four faults are failure to believe the Messenger, failure to pray before God, denial, and turning away from prayer; strutting predated denial.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r8.anchor: فترك التصديق خصلة، والتكذيب خصلة، وترك الصلاة خصلة، والتولي عن الله تعالى خصلة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r10.claim: One occasion report says the Prophet met Abu Jahl by the Banu Makhzum gate, took and shook his hand, and threatened him; Abu Jahl boasted of his status, and the words were revealed as spoken.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r10.anchor: فاستقبله أبو جهل على باب المسجد، مما يلي باب بني مخزوم، فأخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده

QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r11.claim: Qurtubi calls awlā a word of threat and cites a poem repeating it.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:32-35/r11.anchor: وهي كلمة وعيد. قال الشاعر: فأولى ثم أولى ثم أولى

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r1.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r1.claim: Qatada reports Abu Jahl swaggering as the Prophet took his hand and warned him; Abu Jahl said neither the Prophet nor his Lord could harm him, but he was killed miserably at Badr.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r1.anchor: أبو جهل بن هشام يتبختر، فأخذ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بيده

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r2.claim: One view glosses awlā as woe to you, supported by al-Khansāʾ’s poem.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه: الويل لك ومنه قول الخنساء: هممت بنفسي كل الهموم

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r3.claim: On the woe view, it means woe in life, at death, resurrection and Hell; Qurtubi calls this weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r3.anchor: والمعنى: الويل لك حيا، والويل لك ميتا، والويل لك يوم البعث

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r4.claim: Qurtubi rejects as weak the interpretation that awlā means woe repeated through life, death, resurrection and Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r4.anchor: وهذا التكرير كما قال: لك الويلات إنك مرجلي

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r5.claim: Another view takes the phrase to mean condemnation is more fitting than withholding it, with a completion omitted because the expression is frequent.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه الذم لك أولى من تركه، إلا أنه كثير في الكلام فحذف

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r6.claim: A further view says the addressee is more deserving and suited to punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r6.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أنت أولى وأجدر بهذا العذاب

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r7.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r7.claim: Al-Asmaʿi says awlā means approaching destruction, from the root for nearness.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r7.anchor: قال الأصمعي: «أولى» في كلام العرب معناه مقاربة الهلاك

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r8.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r8.claim: Al-Asmaʿi cites poems using awlā for something that has nearly come or is near to afflicting a person.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r8.anchor: وأنشد الأصمعي: وأولى أن يكون له الولاء

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r9.speaker: ثعلب
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r9.claim: Thaʿlab praises al-Asmaʿi’s explanation as unmatched.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r9.anchor: وكان أبو العباس ثعلب يستحسن قول الأصمعي

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r10.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r10.claim: Al-Nahhas glosses awlā laka as nearly perishing then escaping, with destruction closer or more fitting.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r10.anchor: النحاس: العرب تقول أولى لك: كدت تهلك ثم أفلت

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r11.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r11.claim: Al-Mahdawi says awlā is not a comparative but predicates an omitted subject; Abu Zayd’s feminine form shows it is not an elative.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r11.anchor: المهدوي قال: ولا تكون أولى أفعل منك، وتكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r12.claim: On this analysis, laka is the predicate; awlā is indeclinable because it became a proper name for a threat, like Aḥmad.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r12.anchor: فدخول علامة التأنيث دليل على أنه ليس كذلك. و«لك» خبر عن «أولى».

QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r13.claim: Another explanation distributes the repeated threat across the first, second, third and fourth bad deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:34-35/r13.anchor: وقيل: التكرير فيه على معنى ألزم لك على عملك السيىء الأول

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292#2/r1.claim: The expression أولى is a threat and warning, as in the repeated wording in the Resurrection sūra and فأولى لهم in 47:20.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292#2/r1.anchor: أولى: تهدد ووعيد، قال الله تعالى: أولى لك فأولى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292#2/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292#2/r3.claim: The anonymous poet repeats أولى as a threat to a defeated person, supporting the expression’s warning sense.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p292#2/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر لمنهزم : ألفيتا عيناك عند القفا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r1.claim: Awlā laka is a rebuke and threat, derived from w-l-y, nearness; its comparative form signals that destruction is close.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r1.anchor: (أولى لك) عبارة تقال على جهة الزجر والتوعّد والتهديد، واشتقاقها من (الوَلي)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r2.claim: Wayl is an invocation that misfortune befall them; it suits their preference for immediate worldly life and hastening sins while delaying obedience.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r2.anchor: (الويل) كلمة دعاء عليهم بأن يليهم المكروه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r3.claim: The phrase is used at death and in the death throes because punishment is near at that stage.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p683/r3.anchor: وكلمة (أولى) بعد الموت وفي النزع لأن العذاب يكون قريباً منه في هذه المرحلة.

ITQAN:v2p459/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p459/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p459/r1.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ treats أولى لك as a formula of threat and warning and cites a line repeating أولى له.
ITQAN:v2p459/r1.anchor: في قوله تعالى ﴿ أولى لك فأولى ﴾ وفي قوله تعالى ﴿ فأولى لهم ﴾ قال في الصحاح

ITQAN:v2p459/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p459/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
ITQAN:v2p459/r2.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī explains the phrase as danger drawing near or having arrived; al-Jawharī calls this the best explanation.
ITQAN:v2p459/r2.anchor: قال الأصمعي فمعناه قاربه ما يهلكه أي نزل به

ITQAN:v2p459/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p459/r3.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v2p459/r3.claim: Some analyze أولى as an indeclinable verb-like noun meaning evil after evil is near you, with لك as an explanatory phrase.
ITQAN:v2p459/r3.anchor: وقال قوم هو اسم فعل مبني ومعناه وليك شر بعد شر ولك تبيين

ITQAN:v2p459/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p459/r4.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v2p459/r4.claim: Another analysis treats أولى as an indeclinable proper name of threat, nominative as subject with لك as predicate; its pattern is disputed.
ITQAN:v2p459/r4.anchor: وقيل هو علم للوعيد غير مصروف ولذا لم ينون وإن محله رفع على الابتداء

ITQAN:v2p459/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p459/r5.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v2p459/r5.claim: A proposed derivation makes أولى a reversal of ويل لك, from an original أويل, supported by al-Khansāʾ's verse.
ITQAN:v2p459/r5.anchor: وقيل معناه الويل لك وأنه مقلوب منه والأصل أويل فأخر حرف العلة ومنه قول الخنساء

ITQAN:v2p459/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p459/r6.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v2p459/r6.claim: Other explanations are that blame suits you better than leaving it, or that you are more deserving of this punishment.
ITQAN:v2p459/r6.anchor: وقيل معناه الذم لك أولى من تركه فحذف المبتدأ لكثرة دورانه في الكلام

ITQAN:v2p459/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p459/r7.speaker: ثعلب
ITQAN:v2p459/r7.claim: Thaʿlab glosses أولى لك as nearing destruction, from al-waly meaning nearness, and compares الذين يلونكم.
ITQAN:v2p459/r7.anchor: وقال ثعلب أولى لك في كلام العرب معناه مقاربة الهلاك كأنه يقول

ITQAN:v2p459/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p459/r8.speaker: النحاس
ITQAN:v2p459/r8.claim: Al-Naḥḥās explains أولى لك as you nearly perished, with الهلكة understood after لك.
ITQAN:v2p459/r8.anchor: وقال النحاس العرب تقول أولى لك أي كدت تهلك وكأن تقديره أولى لك الهلكة
